2. Verify identity, group composition and inverseAt time zero the sine vanishes and cosine is one. Expanding Φ_s(Φ_tz), the cosine and sine addition formulas identify both coordinates with Φ_{s+t}z; division is legitimate because √η≠0. Taking s=−t or t=−s yields both inverse identities. All times are real, with no domain restriction.cos⁡(s+t)=cos⁡scos⁡t−sin⁡ssin⁡t,sin⁡(s+t)=sin⁡scos⁡t+cos⁡ssin⁡t,Φ−tΦt=ΦtΦ−t=id.Corresponding Lean step  have hzero (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : Φ y xRef 0 z = z := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp [Φ]
    · simp only [Real.cos_zero, Real.sin_zero, one_smul, mul_zero, zero_smul, add_zero]
      module
    · simp
  have hgroup (y xRef : E) (s t : ℝ) (z : E × E) :
      Φ y xRef (s + t) z = Φ y xRef s (Φ y xRef t z) := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> dsimp [Φ]
    all_goal
